items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section VIII, List of Answers on Topics 79:1
items.html: For the Malchut of the Rosh, which is the aspect of the Emanator, since a coupling by striking took place in the screen within her — meaning the aspect of opposition to clothing — she is thus utterly opposite to the aspect of clothing, called the emanated being. And how is it possible for the one to cascade from the other? Hence the Rosh called Keter is considered in two aspects: the first is the aspect of Atik, whose matter is the aspect of opposition to clothing; it is considered only a root for the light of Hassadim, in which the matter of clothing does not apply, since no restriction whatsoever occurred over the light of Hassadim, and the matter of clothing does not coarsen it at all. It is also considered the root of the second Rosh, which is the aspect of AA, whose matter is the aspect of a root for clothing; it is considered an intermediary between the Emanator and the emanated being, being a root for the clothing of the light of Hochma — unlike the Emanator, who is Atik, who is opposite to the aspect of the emanated being, as explained. Hence Keter as a whole is divided into two aspects: Atik, which is a root only for the light of Hassadim, and AA, which is a root for the light of Hochma. (Inner Observation, item 8, Sub Header, “Hence”)
